propositions: Primary watcher (mirror-guard.yml workflow) fails on single instantaneous SHA sample of expected post-submit replication lag; secondary watcher (CloudWatch alarm) has a 2x5-min sustained-divergence window that never alerts on transient lag.

Module docstring (lines 47-50, commit d96628c9dca) states transient divergence (~15s post-submit) is expected and the alarm layer must absorb it via an evaluation window; the workflow's single-sample behavior contradicts this designed capability.

Root cause is incomplete-implementation: the designed lag-absorption window was never built on the workflow surface, shipping as part of a774's introducing commit without implementation on the primary watcher.

Fix adds in-process portable `_replication_check_with_lag_tolerance` wrapper to src/rebar/mirror_guard.py: re-samples up to 3 times (default 45s apart, ~90s window ~6x documented lag) and returns healthy if convergence occurs; unhealthy if divergence persists (no weakening of failure set).

Behavioral change: diverged-then-converged sequence now exits 0 (today exits 1); static/moving persistent divergence still exits 1; in-sync or missing-SHA first sample exits immediately (no re-sampling).

Caller impact is scoped: only the workflow (comment-only update), unit tests (new behavioral tests added), and internal credential-boundary suites — no external or semantic dependency on single-sample failure.
